_comment: The milestone ladder every customer starts from: seven steps, in order, each with what done looks like. The lead and the customer may change the objectives for that customer; the steps are the shared shape, so progress across the batch can be read in one table. Rendered on /milestones/ and on every customer page by admin/build/gen_customers.py. The word is steps.

steps.title: In, with credit
steps.objective: The customer is on the list, has read the start-here page, and has credit to spend on the site.
steps.done_when: The lead has recorded the start date and the credit granted; the customer has said which agent they will start with.

steps.title: One agent named
steps.objective: One agent in one deployment, named: what it is (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, a connector, a scheduled job), where it runs, and what it holds.
steps.done_when: A sentence on the customer page names the agent and the shape it is nearest to in the sixteen published examples.

steps.title: The grant, measured or documented
steps.objective: What the agent can actually reach, one row per capability, in the pinned vocabulary.
steps.done_when: A grant.json exists for the agent, measured where the customer is entitled to run a probe and documented from the vendor's pages where not, with dates.
steps.who: the customer's agent, from MAP-A-GRANT.md or the try-it prompts

steps.title: The mandate, in the customer's words
steps.objective: What the customer actually wants the agent to do, what they refuse, and what they never thought to mention.
steps.done_when: A mandate.json exists with want, do_not_want and unstated, drafted by the agent and corrected by the customer. The correction is the elicitation.

steps.title: The delta, and the first finding
steps.objective: The gap between the grant and the mandate: the excess, the unbounded excess, and what stands in the way of each row.
steps.done_when: The customer page records the row count and the gap count, and the customer has named one row that surprised them.
steps.who: derived by the build; read by the customer

steps.title: The hooks half: what the harness holds
steps.objective: The part of the behaviour policy the agent's harness can hold as hooks or rules, so an expectation becomes a setting or a boundary where one exists.
steps.done_when: The rows that the harness can hold are marked, the hooks or rules for them exist in the customer's deployment, and the rest are marked honestly as expectations.
steps.who: the customer, with the follow-up; the agent writes the first draft

steps.title: The usage moment
steps.objective: The moment the behaviour policy became worth something to this customer: what it was, what they used of the credit, and whether they topped up.
steps.done_when: The customer has said in their own words what it is worth and what a fair price would be, and the follow-up has recorded credit used and whether they topped up.
steps.who: the customer; recorded by the follow-up
